yt-dlp.whenToUse: Download video and audio from thousands of sites, with format selection and playlists.
yt-dlp.whenNotToUse: For image galleries gallery-dl handles more sites.
gotchas: Needs ffmpeg on PATH to merge separate video and audio streams.
Extractors break when sites change. Update before reporting a failure.

ffmpeg.whenToUse: Convert, cut, resize or re-encode audio and video. The tool everything else wraps.
ffmpeg.whenNotToUse: To download from a site use yt-dlp, which calls ffmpeg for you.
gotchas: Argument order matters: options before -i apply to the input, after it to the output.
-c copy remuxes without re-encoding and is orders of magnitude faster when it applies.
usages: ffmpeg -i input.mp4 output.mp3  # Convert video to audio
ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -ss 00:00:10 -to 00:00:20 -c copy cut.mp4  # Cut clip
ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf scale=1280:-1 out.mp4  # Resize video

mpv.whenToUse: Play a video or audio file, including straight from a URL.
mpv.whenNotToUse: To convert or cut rather than watch, use ffmpeg.
gotchas: Can play a yt-dlp URL directly, but only when yt-dlp is on PATH.

gallery-dl.whenToUse: Download image galleries and artist archives, with site-specific naming rules.
gotchas: Many sites need credentials or cookies in gallery-dl.conf before anything downloads.

fd.whenToUse: Find files by name. Sensible defaults, regex by default, and it respects .gitignore.
fd.whenNotToUse: To act on the results in a pipeline of PowerShell objects, Get-ChildItem gives you objects.
gotchas: Debian and Ubuntu install the binary as fdfind to avoid a name clash. Alias fd to it.

rg.whenToUse: Search code recursively. Respects .gitignore, skips binaries, and is the fastest option here.
rg.whenNotToUse: To match a literal string with regex metacharacters in it, pass -F.
gotchas: Honours .gitignore by default, so it will silently skip ignored files. Pass -u, -uu or -uuu to widen.

ripgrep.whenToUse: The package name for rg. Install this; run rg.
ripgrep.whenNotToUse: Do not type ripgrep at a prompt: the binary is called rg.
gotchas: ripgrep is the package; rg is the command.
Not a Windows builtin. Git for Windows may ship grep.exe; prefer findstr or Select-String on Windows PowerShell.
grep.whenToUse: POSIX recursive text search when rg is not installed.
grep.whenNotToUse: On Windows PowerShell prefer findstr.exe or Select-String; rg covers both.

gotchas: Use findstr.exe. PowerShell find is not this command.
findstr.whenToUse: Search file contents on Windows without installing rg.
findstr.whenNotToUse: Use Select-String for objects in the pipeline, or rg for speed and Unicode.

jq.whenToUse: Query and reshape JSON on the command line. The default answer for JSON in a pipeline.
jq.whenNotToUse: For an interactive look at an unfamiliar document, fx is easier to explore with.
gotchas: Single quotes do not quote in cmd.exe. In PowerShell and cmd, wrap filters in double quotes and escape inner ones.
usages: jq -r '.[] | .name' file.json   # Raw strings from array

yq.whenToUse: Query YAML with jq syntax, and convert between YAML, JSON and TOML.
yq.whenNotToUse: For JSON only, jq is the more widely installed tool.
gotchas: Two unrelated programs are called yq. The Go one (mikefarah) takes eval; the Python wrapper takes jq syntax directly.
usages: yq -o json file.yaml            # Convert YAML to JSON

fx.whenToUse: Explore an unfamiliar JSON document interactively, folding and unfolding as you go.
fx.whenNotToUse: In a script or a pipeline use jq; fx is built around a TTY.

git.whenToUse: Version control. Everything else in this category is a friendlier front end to it.
git.whenNotToUse: Nothing substitutes for it; lazygit, tig and gh all drive git underneath.
usages: git switch -c <branch>          # Create and switch branch

gh.whenToUse: Do GitHub things from the terminal: pull requests, issues, releases, CI runs.
gh.whenNotToUse: For anything that touches commits and branches, use git.
gotchas: Needs gh auth login first. In CI, set GH_TOKEN instead.
usages: gh repo view                    # Show current repo
gh pr create                    # Open a pull request

delta.whenToUse: Make git diff readable: syntax highlighting, side-by-side, and word-level changes.
delta.whenNotToUse: It is a pager for git, not a standalone differ. For two loose files use diff.
gotchas: Does nothing until git is configured to use it as core.pager and interactive.diffFilter.
usages: git diff | delta                # Highlighted git diff
delta file.old file.new         # Compare two files

lazygit.whenToUse: Stage hunks, rebase, and resolve conflicts in a terminal UI, without memorising git flags.
lazygit.whenNotToUse: In a script or over a pipe use git; lazygit needs a TTY.

tig.whenToUse: Browse git history and blame in a terminal pager, commit by commit.
tig.whenNotToUse: To stage, commit or rebase interactively, lazygit does more.

httpie.whenToUse: Call an HTTP API with readable syntax and coloured, pretty-printed JSON responses.
httpie.whenNotToUse: In CI or a Dockerfile curl is already present and needs no Python.
gotchas: httpie is the package; the command is http. On Debian it may install as http or httpie depending on version.
usages: http POST https://api.example.com name=cmdpeek  # Form POST

http.whenToUse: The command HTTPie installs. Sends JSON by default and pretty-prints the response.
http.whenNotToUse: In CI or a Dockerfile curl is already present and needs no Python.
gotchas: Clashes with other tools named http on PATH. httpie also installs https for TLS-by-default.
usages: http POST :8080/api id:=1       # JSON POST to localhost

gotchas: In Windows PowerShell, curl is an alias for Invoke-WebRequest. Call curl.exe for the real client.
curl.whenToUse: HTTP from any OS, including Windows 10+ System32 curl.exe.
curl.whenNotToUse: Do not rely on the curl alias inside Windows PowerShell.

wget.whenToUse: Download a file or mirror a site, with retries and resume built in.
wget.whenNotToUse: For API calls with headers and methods, curl or httpie read better.
gotchas: Not present on macOS by default, and Windows PowerShell aliases wget to Invoke-WebRequest. Call wget.exe.

aria2c.whenToUse: Download large files fast by opening several connections, and resume when they break.
aria2c.whenNotToUse: For a small file or an API call the extra connections buy nothing; use curl.
gotchas: Some servers rate-limit or reject multi-connection downloads. Drop -x if transfers fail.

7z.whenToUse: Extract or create almost any archive format, including rar and 7z that tar cannot read.
7z.whenNotToUse: For plain .tar.gz on a POSIX box tar is already there and needs no install.
gotchas: The binary is 7z on Linux and 7z.exe on Windows; some Scoop manifests install it as 7zz.

tar.whenToUse: Pack or unpack .tar, .tar.gz and .tar.xz. Present on Windows 10+ as well as every POSIX box.
gotchas: Windows bsdtar does not support --same-owner or the GNU long option spellings.
usages: tar -czf archive.tar.gz folder  # Create gzip tarball

bat.whenToUse: Read a file with syntax highlighting, line numbers, and git gutter marks.
bat.whenNotToUse: When piping into another program use cat, or pass --plain, since bat paginates by default.
gotchas: Debian and Ubuntu install the binary as batcat.
Pipes to a pager when the output is a TTY. Use --paging=never in scripts.
usages: bat file.ps1                    # Print file with syntax highlighting

less.whenToUse: Page through long output, search inside it, and scroll backwards.
less.whenNotToUse: For a file you want highlighted, bat is nicer when installed.
gotchas: Windows PowerShell has no less; more.com is the builtin equivalent.
usages: less file.txt                   # Page through a file
less +F logfile                 # Follow a growing file

fzf.whenToUse: Filter any list interactively. Pipe something in, pick something out.
fzf.whenNotToUse: In a script with no TTY it will hang waiting for input; use rg or fd filters instead.
gotchas: Shell keybindings (Ctrl-R, Ctrl-T) need the fzf key-bindings script sourced in your profile.
usages: fd | fzf                        # Pick a file from fd results

eza.whenToUse: A directory listing with colour, icons, git status, and a tree mode.
eza.whenNotToUse: In scripts parse nothing; use fd or Get-ChildItem.
gotchas: The successor to exa, which is unmaintained. Flags are close but not identical.
usages: eza -la --git                   # All files with git status

lsd.whenToUse: An ls replacement with colour and icons, and closer to ls flags than eza.
lsd.whenNotToUse: In scripts parse nothing; use fd or Get-ChildItem.

docker.whenNotToUse: For a Kubernetes cluster use kubectl; docker only sees the local daemon.
gotchas: Needs a running daemon. On Windows and macOS that means Docker Desktop or an equivalent VM.
docker-compose (hyphen) is the old v1 binary. Current syntax is docker compose.
usages: docker run --rm -it alpine      # Run ephemeral container
docker compose up -d            # Start compose stack

lazydocker.whenToUse: Watch and manage local containers, images and logs in a terminal UI.
lazydocker.whenNotToUse: In a script use docker; lazydocker needs a TTY.

dive.whenToUse: See what each layer of an image adds, and find the wasted space.
dive.whenNotToUse: To run or build images use docker.

kubectl.whenToUse: Talk to a Kubernetes cluster: inspect, apply, log, exec.
kubectl.whenNotToUse: For local single-host containers use docker.
gotchas: Acts on the current kubeconfig context. Check kubectl config current-context before anything destructive.

helm.whenToUse: Install and upgrade packaged Kubernetes applications, with values files and rollback.
helm.whenNotToUse: For a handful of plain manifests kubectl apply is less machinery.
gotchas: Helm 2 needed a cluster-side Tiller; Helm 3 does not. Old guides will not match.

k9s.whenToUse: Browse and act on a live cluster in a terminal UI, with logs and shells one key away.
k9s.whenNotToUse: In a script use kubectl; k9s needs a TTY.

terraform.whenToUse: Declare and apply infrastructure. The original, now under a source-available licence.
terraform.whenNotToUse: If the licence matters to you, opentofu is the MPL fork and takes the same config.
gotchas: State is authoritative. Never edit it by hand, and never run apply against a state you do not own.

opentofu.whenToUse: The MPL-licensed fork of Terraform. Same HCL, same providers, open licence.
opentofu.whenNotToUse: A team already standardised on terraform should stay there; mixing state between them is risky.
gotchas: The binary is tofu, not opentofu.

packer.whenToUse: Build identical machine images for several platforms from one template.
packer.whenNotToUse: To provision running infrastructure use terraform or opentofu.

node.whenToUse: Run JavaScript and TypeScript tooling outside a browser.
node.whenNotToUse: To switch between project Node versions use fnm rather than reinstalling node.

pnpm.whenToUse: Install Node dependencies with a content-addressed store, so repeated installs are near instant.
pnpm.whenNotToUse: A repo with a committed package-lock.json or yarn.lock expects that tool instead.
usages: pnpm run <script>               # Run a package script

yarn.whenToUse: Install Node dependencies in a repo that has a yarn.lock.
yarn.whenNotToUse: Do not mix with npm or pnpm in the same repo; the lockfiles disagree.
gotchas: Yarn 1 and Yarn 2+ (Berry) take different commands. Check the packageManager field in package.json.

fnm.whenToUse: Install and switch Node versions per directory, driven by .node-version or .nvmrc.
fnm.whenNotToUse: If you only ever need one Node version, installing node directly is simpler.
gotchas: Needs a shell hook (fnm env) in your profile before cd will switch versions.
usages: fnm install --lts               # Install latest LTS Node

python.whenToUse: Run Python and its stdlib tooling, including venv and http.server.
python.whenNotToUse: On Windows the launcher py picks the right version; on Debian the binary is python3.
gotchas: Debian and Ubuntu ship no bare python. Call python3, or install python-is-python3.

uv.whenToUse: Create venvs and resolve Python dependencies. Much faster than pip, and it can install Python itself.
uv.whenNotToUse: For installing a standalone Python CLI, pipx keeps each tool isolated.
usages: uv pip install requests         # Install package
uv run script.py                # Run in project env

pipx.whenToUse: Install a Python CLI into its own virtualenv so it cannot break another tool.
pipx.whenNotToUse: For a library your project imports use uv or pip inside the project venv.
gotchas: pipx install puts the binary in ~/.local/bin, which is not on PATH by default. Run pipx ensurepath once.
usages: pipx install <pkg>              # Install CLI in isolated env

py.whenToUse: Pick a Python version on Windows without juggling PATH: py -3.12 runs that interpreter.
py.whenNotToUse: Not present on Linux or macOS.
gotchas: Reads py.ini and the #! line of the script, so py script.py may not use the version you expect.

nvim.whenToUse: Vim with Lua config, LSP, and treesitter built in.
nvim.whenNotToUse: On a machine you do not own, vim is the one that will already be installed.
gotchas: Ignores ~/.vimrc. Config lives in ~/.config/nvim (or $LOCALAPPDATA/nvim on Windows).

vim.whenToUse: Edit a file over SSH or on a box where nothing else is installed.
vim.whenNotToUse: For a configured editing setup, nvim or helix need much less work.
gotchas: Exit is :q, or :q! to discard changes.
usages: vim +'set nu' file.txt          # Open with line numbers

helix.whenToUse: A modal editor with LSP and treesitter working out of the box, no plugins to wire up.
helix.whenNotToUse: Vim muscle memory does not transfer: helix is selection-first, so the verb comes last.
gotchas: The binary is hx, not helix.

just.whenToUse: Keep a project command list in a justfile and run it by name. Make without the build semantics.
just.whenNotToUse: For actual incremental builds with file dependencies, use make.

make.whenToUse: Run build steps with dependency tracking. Present almost everywhere.
make.whenNotToUse: For a plain list of project commands with no file dependencies, just is far less fiddly.
gotchas: Recipe lines must be indented with a tab. Spaces produce "missing separator".
Not present on Windows by default; install it or use just.

watchexec.whenToUse: Rerun a command whenever files change.
watchexec.whenNotToUse: For a watcher your framework already ships (vite, cargo watch, dotnet watch), use that.
gotchas: Watches the whole working directory, so a build that writes into it can trigger itself. Use --ignore.
usages: watchexec -e rs cargo test      # Watch Rust files

hyperfine.whenToUse: Benchmark commands properly: warmup runs, several samples, and a statistical comparison.
hyperfine.whenNotToUse: For a one-off wall-clock number, time or Measure-Command is enough.
usages: hyperfine -w 3 'cmd a' 'cmd b'  # Compare two commands

tokei.whenToUse: Count lines of code per language across a tree, fast.
tokei.whenNotToUse: For a line count of one file, wc -l is already there.

sd.whenToUse: Find and replace across files with plain regex syntax, without sed dialect differences.
sd.whenNotToUse: For stream editing beyond substitution, sed still has the full command language.
gotchas: sd rewrites files in place with no backup. Check the diff first, or run under git.
usages: sd <find> <replace> file        # Replace in a file

dust.whenToUse: See which directories are eating the disk, as a sorted tree.
dust.whenNotToUse: For the size of one path in a script, du -sh or Get-ChildItem measure is easier to parse.

zoxide.whenToUse: Jump to a directory you have visited before by a fragment of its name.
zoxide.whenNotToUse: It only knows directories you have already cd-ed into, so it is useless on a fresh machine.
gotchas: Needs a shell init line (zoxide init) in your profile before z works.

rclone.whenToUse: Copy or sync files to and from cloud storage: S3, Google Drive, Dropbox, and dozens more.
rclone.whenNotToUse: For a plain HTTP download use curl or wget; rclone wants a configured remote.
gotchas: rclone sync deletes files at the destination that are gone from the source. Dry-run with --dry-run first.
usages: rclone copy src dest            # Copy files

sqlite3.whenToUse: Query or create a SQLite database file with no server to run.
sqlite3.whenNotToUse: For Postgres or MySQL use their own clients; the SQL dialects differ.
gotchas: Without a trailing semicolon the shell waits for more input rather than running your statement.

pwsh.whenToUse: PowerShell 7 or later: cross-platform, and the version cmdpeek itself targets for new work.
pwsh.whenNotToUse: A script that needs Windows-only modules or WinPS 5.1 behaviour should run in powershell.exe.
gotchas: pwsh and powershell are different shells with different module paths and different default encodings.

gsudo.whenToUse: Run one command elevated on Windows without opening a new admin window.
gsudo.whenNotToUse: Not a POSIX sudo: it elevates, it does not switch users.
gotchas: Still shows a UAC prompt unless cached. gsudo cache on reduces the prompting.
usages: gsudo config CacheMode Auto     # Cache credentials

starship.whenToUse: A prompt that shows git state, language versions and exit codes, in any shell.
starship.whenNotToUse: It only draws the prompt; it changes nothing about how commands run.
gotchas: Needs an init line in your shell profile, and a Nerd Font for the default glyphs.
usages: starship init powershell        # Print profile snippet

winget.whenToUse: Install software on Windows from the Microsoft Store and the community repo. Ships with Windows 10 1809+.
winget.whenNotToUse: For a per-user developer toolchain scoop updates faster and needs no elevation.
gotchas: Package ids are case sensitive and often vendor-prefixed, as in BurntSushi.ripgrep.MSVC.

scoop.whenToUse: Install developer CLIs on Windows per user, with no elevation and no installers.
scoop.whenNotToUse: For system-wide software, drivers or MSIs use choco or winget.
gotchas: Shims live in ~/scoop/shims. A shell opened before the first install will not have it on PATH.

choco.whenToUse: Install Windows software machine-wide, including MSI installers and drivers scoop will not touch.
choco.whenNotToUse: For a per-user install with no elevation prefer scoop.
gotchas: Install and upgrade need an elevated shell. gsudo choco install works from a normal one.

brew.whenToUse: Install CLI tools on macOS, and on Linux when you want newer versions than apt ships.
brew.whenNotToUse: On Windows use winget or scoop.
gotchas: Apple Silicon installs under /opt/homebrew, Intel under /usr/local. A shell that predates the install will not see it.

apt.whenToUse: Install and query system packages on Debian and Ubuntu.
apt.whenNotToUse: Not present on Windows or macOS. Use winget, scoop or brew there.
gotchas: Needs sudo for install and remove. apt is for humans; apt-get is the one to script against.
Windows find.exe searches file contents (like findstr), not names. Use Get-ChildItem or fd for names on Windows.
find.whenToUse: Walk a POSIX directory tree by name, type, or mtime.
find.whenNotToUse: On Windows use fd, Get-ChildItem, or where.exe — not find.exe.

gotchas: PowerShell ls is Get-ChildItem, not POSIX ls. Flags like -la do not mean the same thing.
ls.whenNotToUse: In PowerShell prefer Get-ChildItem or eza/lsd when installed.

npm.whenToUse: Install Node dependencies and run package scripts. Ships with node.
npm.whenNotToUse: pnpm is faster and uses far less disk for the same lockfile.
gotchas: npm install rewrites package-lock.json. Use npm ci in CI to install exactly the lockfile.
usages: npm run <script>                # Run a package script

python3.whenToUse: The Python binary name that actually exists on Linux and macOS.
python3.whenNotToUse: On Windows use py or python; python3 there is often a Store stub that only opens the Store.
